assumed_value: your firm factor 0.5 accepted as declared, unchecked against the battery's energy
why_it_binds: a battery is firm only for what its stored energy can sustain: with no energy rating its firm credit is the same whatever its size, so the capacity it adds to the envelope is unchecked
how_to_get_it: the battery datasheet or supplier quotation: usable energy in MWh at the discharge rate the duty needs

assumed_value: credited at nameplate x firm factor, as if no unit could be out of service
why_it_binds: firm capacity under N+1 is what is left after the largest unit is lost: the same capacity is none of it as one unit, half as two, three quarters as four. Nameplate alone cannot say which it is
how_to_get_it: the generator schedule: how many units make up the option's capacity_MW, and the redundancy scheme your resilience design requires (N, N+1, N+2 or 2N)

why_it_binds: When absent, the hybrid and full-DLC scenarios ASSUME three 1,350 kW N+1 CDUs already installed at no cost, which supplies roughly 22 racks of liquid capacity that the hall may not have.
how_to_get_it: CDU nameplates and the mechanical single-line diagram.

input: Flow the existing hall already draws on the plant
assumed_value: 0 l/min, nothing subtracted (the pumped flow is read as flow available to the new load)
why_it_binds: If the available pumped flow above is the plant's TOTAL, the existing hall already uses part of it and the hydraulic limit is overstated. When this is given the engine subtracts it before dividing by the flow per rack; when absent nothing is subtracted and the figure above is read as flow available to the new load.
how_to_get_it: Commissioning flow readings or the BMS flow trend for the existing hall's loops; pump curves at the operating point.

input: Other heat the existing hall already puts on the plant
assumed_value: 0 kW, nothing subtracted (plant headroom is the plant capacity less the IT load only)
why_it_binds: Plant headroom is the capacity less the IT load; UPS and distribution losses, fan-wall and pump power rejected to the plant and lighting also land on it, so headroom is overstated by their share. When this is given the engine subtracts it as well; when absent only the IT load is subtracted.
how_to_get_it: BMS plant load trend less the metered IT load, or the electrical single-line losses and the mechanical schedule's fan and pump power.

why_it_binds: Whether the plant can hold the water temperature the chips need.
how_to_get_it: The platform vendor's reference design for the target rack.

input: Rear-door heat exchanger capacity per rack
why_it_binds: Decides whether the rear-door scenario can host the target rack at all. When absent the engine uses a library default of 60 kW per rack (band 20-80), which is neither a manufacturer's rating nor a site measurement.
how_to_get_it: The selected rear-door unit's datasheet at the site's water temperature and airflow.

why_it_binds: Every annual energy cost, cost per GPU-hour and lifecycle figure is priced at this. When absent the engine uses a 140 EUR/MWh placeholder (band 90-220).
how_to_get_it: The supply contract, or 12 months of invoices divided by metered energy.

assumed_value: none: the lifecycle value is undiscounted
why_it_binds: When absent the lifecycle value is stated undiscounted and says so.

assumed_value: 0 kW, nothing subtracted (busway_ampacity_A is read as the whole installed total)
why_it_binds: The busway result is the installed capacity as declared; the load already drawing from it is not subtracted, so the racks it can still feed are overstated by that share. When this is given the engine subtracts it (never below zero); when absent nothing is subtracted.
how_to_get_it: Branch-circuit or busway monitoring (peak kW over a representative month), or the sum of the metered rack loads on the busway.
